title: Global Verdier duality
statement:
Let $X$ be smooth, separated of finite type and geometrically connected of
pure dimension $d$ over $k$ (no admissibility hypothesis on $a_X$: its
exceptional adjoint is the unconditional one of [sk-def-sf-operations](vi)).
Assume either that $X$ is proper, or that
$X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$ for a smooth, separated finite-type, geometrically
connected $k_0$-scheme $X_0$; in the latter case no properness is required.
For $K\in\Dctf(X,\Lambda)$ there is a canonical isomorphism

$$
\RG_c(X,K)^\vee\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\RG\bigl(X,\mathbb D_XK\bigr),
$$

in the point category $\Dbc(s,\Lambda)$ of def:weil-finite-coefficient-point,
natural in $K\in\Dctf(X,\Lambda)$ and compatible with finite reduction, scalar
extension and shifts; for $K=\Lambda_X$ it reads
$\RG_c(X,\Lambda)^\vee\cong\RG(X,\omega_X)$.

proof.text: Put $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$, $a=a_X:X\to s$, $C=Ra_!K$ and $B=Ra_*\mathbb D_XK$, using [sk-def-sf-operations] and the dualizing-object and duality notation of [def-sf-pf]. The hypotheses make $a$ a separated finite-type morphism between separated finite-type $k$-schemes. The coefficient unit has finite Tor amplitude $[0,0]$. Apply [thm-sf-ctf-stability](v) to the unit to obtain $\omega_X=Ra^!\Lambda_s\in\Dctf(X,\Lambda)$, then (ii) to $(K,\omega_X)$ to obtain $\mathbb D_XK\in\Dctf(X,\Lambda)$. Clauses (iv) and (iii), applied respectively to $K$ and $\mathbb D_XK$, give $C,B\in\Dctf(s,\Lambda)$. At finite coefficients these are precisely the displayed preservation assertions; clause (vii) supplies their integral, rational and common-stage versions. Apply (v) also to $\operatorname{id}_s$ and $\Lambda_s$ to obtain $\omega_s\in\Dctf(s,\Lambda)$; then (ii) at $s$ puts $\mathbb D_s C=R\mathcal H om_s(C,\omega_s)$ in $\Dctf(s,\Lambda)$. Thus all objects used below lie in the bounded constructible point category, even though the exchange theorem is stated in an ambient category.

source.place: Sole paragraph, before specializing exchange: verify the small-category domains using the existing preservation theorem

proof.text: Apply [sk-thm-sf-verdier-exchange] to $f=a$, $Y=s$ and $M=K$. It gives the canonical isomorphism $\eta_K:\mathbb D_s C\xrightarrow{\sim}B$, natural contravariantly in $K$ and compatible with finite reduction, scalar extension and shifts. Both ends belong to the full bounded constructible subcategory by step 1; the map and its inverse therefore restrict to an isomorphism there. The theorem uses the constructible exceptional adjoint of [sk-def-sf-operations](vi), so its hypotheses require no additional ambient admissibility datum. This application works under either geometric alternative in the item: both supply the same separated finite-type structure morphism.

source.place: Sole paragraph, first sentence: specialize Verdier exchange to the structure morphism

proof.text: Write $F_\Lambda=\operatorname{Fib}_s$. Use the exceptional adjunction of [sk-def-sf-operations](vi) and the counit normalization for the exceptional adjoint of the identity, whose compact-support functor is the identity; thus the point normalization is the adjunction identification, rather than a choice of an arbitrary isomorphism. The point identifications of [lem-sf-point] give $\omega_s\cong\Lambda_s$ and identify the evaluated internal Hom $F_\Lambda\mathbb D_s C$ with $R\operatorname{Hom}_\Lambda(F_\Lambda C,\Lambda)=(F_\Lambda C)^\vee$. The current [lem-sf-point](3) and [lem-weil-point-fibre-equivalence] identify the exact fibre equivalence at each of the four coefficient stages, with targets $D^b_{\mathrm{fin}}(A_{E,n})$, $D^b_{\mathrm{fg}}(\mathcal O_E)$, $D^b_{\mathrm{fd}}(E)$ and the common-stage $D^b_{\mathrm{fd}}(\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell)$ respectively. By [def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology], $F_\Lambda C=R\Gamma_c(X,K)$ and $F_\Lambda B=R\Gamma(X,\mathbb D_XK)$. Define the asserted arrow $\gamma_K$ by composing the inverse of the internal-Hom point identification with $F_\Lambda(\eta_K)$ and these two global-section identifications. Each factor is invertible, so $\gamma_K$ is invertible. Through the fibre equivalence this is the asserted isomorphism in $D^b_c(s,\Lambda)$, not just an isomorphism of cohomology groups.

source.place: Sole paragraph, remaining sentences: evaluate and identify the two sides

proof.text: Make the point internal-Hom comparison of step 3 explicit: [lem-sf-point](2) gives an isomorphism but specifies neither the map nor its naturality. Write $F=F_\Lambda$, $t_{P,Q}:F(P\otimes^L Q)\xrightarrow{\sim}FP\otimes^L FQ$ and $u:F\Lambda_s\xrightarrow{\sim}\Lambda$ for the natural coherent tensor and unit comparisons of [lem-sf-point-fibre-derived-tensor] on finite-Tor point objects, and $e:C\otimes^L\mathbb D_sC\to\Lambda_s$ for internal-Hom evaluation of [sk-def-sf-operations](i) followed by $\omega_s\cong\Lambda_s$ of [lem-sf-point](1). Define $\alpha_C:F\mathbb D_sC\to R\operatorname{Hom}_\Lambda(FC,\Lambda)$ as the module tensor/Hom transpose of $u\circ Fe\circ t_{C,\mathbb D_sC}^{-1}:FC\otimes^L F\mathbb D_sC\to\Lambda$. Invertibility: $C$, $\mathbb D_sC$ (step 1) and $\Lambda_s[-r]$ lie in $\Dctf(s,\Lambda)$, so both ends are bounded. For each $r$, under [lem-sf-point](5) and the module adjunction, $H^r(\alpha_C)$ is the composite of the bijections $\operatorname{Hom}_s(\Lambda_s[-r],\mathbb D_sC)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_s(\Lambda_s[-r]\otimes^L C,\Lambda_s)$ (adjunction (i)), then $F$ (fully faithful and shift-compatible by [lem-weil-point-fibre-equivalence]), then $t$ and $u$, then $\operatorname{Hom}_\Lambda(\Lambda[-r]\otimes^L FC,\Lambda)\cong H^r R\operatorname{Hom}_\Lambda(FC,\Lambda)$; they agree by the definition of the transpose and the naturality and unit constraint of $t$. So each $H^r(\alpha_C)$ is bijective and $\alpha_C$ is invertible (at $\Qlb$ at a common finite stage). Naturality in $C$ and the shift squares follow from naturality of $t,u,e$; the finite-reduction and scalar-extension squares hold because $t,u$ commute with them by [lem-sf-point-fibre-derived-tensor] and internal Hom with its evaluation does by [thm-sf-ctf-stability](vii): after the transpose bijection each square is a tensor/unit/evaluation square. This $\alpha_C$ is the identification used in step 3.

source.place: Sole paragraph, canonical point evaluation; make explicit the naturality and coefficient clauses of the statement

proof.text: For integral-to-finite passage, the actual comparison $F_{A_{E,n}}(N\otimes^L A_{E,n})\cong F_{\mathcal O_E}(N)\otimes^L A_{E,n}$ is [lem-pod-point-sections-derived-reduction], applicable because the point objects in step 1 are bounded constructible. The integral and rational scalar comparisons are [lem-weil-point-sections-scalar-extension], including its identity and tower equations; the common-stage definition of [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point] uses these same comparisons for $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$. Thus all point identifications in $\gamma_K$ commute with the comparisons. The exchange factor has these properties by [sk-thm-sf-verdier-exchange]. Composing its naturality or coefficient square with the point-identification squares proves the corresponding square for $\gamma_K$; composing the shift squares gives the contravariant shift convention on both sides. This proves naturality, finite-reduction compatibility, scalar-extension compatibility and shift compatibility of the specified canonical arrow.

source.place: Sole paragraph, canonical point evaluation; make explicit the naturality and coefficient clauses of the statement

proof.text: Take $K=\Lambda_X$, the coefficient object of [def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology] (the coefficient unit $\Lambda_X$ of [def-sf-pf], the tensor unit as in [sk-def-sf-setting]), so that $R\Gamma_c(X,\Lambda)=R\Gamma_c(X,\Lambda_X)$ by the abbreviation of [def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology]. By [def-sf-pf], $\mathbb D_X\Lambda_X=R\mathcal H om_X(\Lambda_X,\omega_X)$. This identifies canonically with $\omega_X$: the adjoint of the tensor unitor $\Lambda_X\otimes^L\omega_X\to\omega_X$ gives $\omega_X\to R\mathcal H om_X(\Lambda_X,\omega_X)$; in the other direction use the inverse left unitor followed by internal-Hom evaluation. The two composites are identities by the tensor/internal-Hom adjunction identities of [sk-def-sf-operations](i). Substitute this identification into $\gamma_{\Lambda_X}$ from step 3 to obtain $R\Gamma_c(X,\Lambda)^\vee\cong R\Gamma(X,\omega_X)$.
